statement: Before recording a review finding as fixed, rerun the finding's own scenario against the fix. Passing tests that were written for something else are not that check. 2026-11-09, #687, my own error: a round-1 review found that npm exec running from the shared $RUNNER_TEMP could read a caller's .npmrc and node_modules there. I changed each step to cd into a fresh mktemp -d directory and recorded the finding as fixed, after checking only that installs still worked. Round 2 showed npm walks up from a directory with no package.json to the nearest parent that has a package.json or node_modules. With a planted $RUNNER_TEMP/node_modules/pnpm reporting 9.0.0 and a planted .npmrc registry, npm used both, and the planted pnpm ran install. Fix: write an empty package.json in the fresh directory first. Rerun against the same plant, npm's prefix was the fresh directory, the default registry was used, and the planted pnpm never ran.
